ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure is a sea-level isobar map of a higher-latitude area in the Northern Hemisphere, marked with the 60° and 70° latitude lines and the 180° meridian. Place 1 is located in the middle-right part of the figure, near a nearly north-south curving isobar; nearby, the 1020 hPa and 1012 hPa isobars can be seen; the pressure values near the southeast side of place 1 are relatively high, and toward the inside on the northwest side there are 1012 hPa and lower 1004 hPa isobars distributed. Reasoning: therefore, the high-pressure side near place 1 is roughly on the southeast side, and the low-pressure side is roughly on the northwest side; the horizontal pressure-gradient force points from southeast to northwest. Place 1 is in the Northern Hemisphere; near-surface wind is deflected to the right on the basis of the pressure-gradient-force direction, and crosses the isobars obliquely toward the low-pressure side. Combined with the directions of the longitude and latitude lines in the figure, the actual wind vector is roughly from southwest to northeast, so the wind direction is named by the direction it comes from as southwesterly wind.
